 health, and besides increasing with greater consumption of fruits 
and vegetables, it also increases with consumption of carotenoid-containing 
nutritional supplements, smoking cessation, and loss of excess body fat 
(Carlson et al., 2006). It has also been found to be lower in those with an 
ongoing oxidative stress such as with metabolic syndrome (Holt et al, 2014). 
RRS has also been used to assess carotenoids in precancerous skin lesions, 
and to assess early stages of macular degeneration in the retina (Carlson 
et al., 2006).
With the development of portable scanners, RRS measurement is quick, 
easy, and inexpensive, making it a possible nutritional assessment tool for 
professionals in the future.
